baseline.name: Materialize both concatenations before comparison
baseline.approach: Allocate str1+str2 and str2+str1, compare them, then copy the gcd-length prefix if equal.
baseline.space: O(n+m) temporary concatenations plus O(g) output

archived.name: Virtual concatenation comparison
archived.time: O(n+m), where n and m are the string lengths; Euclidean length-GCD work is dominated by that scan
archived.space: O(1) explicit auxiliary state plus O(g) returned string, where g=gcd(n,m)

why: Character indexing compares both concatenation orders without constructing temporary strings.
quantitative_comparison: The two temporary concatenations would contain 2(n+m) characters plus terminators. The archive avoids those buffers and their allocations while retaining up to n+m virtual character comparisons. Time growth remains linear; no measured speed factor is established.
tradeoffs: Adds indexing branches and still allocates the output. Strings/length bounds are assumed, and the mismatch path's one-byte allocation is unchecked.
evidence_basis: Static source inspection and stated algorithm work/storage model. Comparator is an analytical alternative, not an implemented or timed benchmark. Historical platform acceptance is separate from current local validation.
